Bayesian stochastic mortality models in Stan (StanMoMo)

Source: R/model-stanmomo.R
stanmomo.Rd

Wrapper around StanMoMo (Barigou, Goffard, Loisel and Salhi 2023): Bayesian versions of the Lee-Carter ("lc"), Renshaw-Haberman ("rh"), age-period-cohort ("apc"), Cairns-Blake-Dowd ("cbd") and M6 ("m6") models, fitted with Stan to the deaths and exposures of each stratum with a Poisson or negative binomial likelihood (log link). Period indexes follow random walks with drift (CBD and M6: correlated), cohort effects AR(2) processes.

Usage

stanmomo(
  model = c("lc", "rh", "apc", "cbd", "m6"),
  family = c("poisson", "nb"),
  h_max = 50,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  cores = 1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

model

"lc", "rh", "apc", "cbd" or "m6".

family

"poisson" or "nb" (negative binomial).

h_max

Longest forecast horizon the fit supports (at least 2).

chains, iter

Number of Markov chains and iterations per chain (half of them warm-up).

cores

Cores for the chains.

seed

Seed of the sampler; NULL draws one from R's random number generator, so that set.seed() makes fits reproducible.

Value

A model specification.

Details

StanMoMo forecasts inside the fit, so the model is fitted with forecasts up to h_max years. Draws are posterior draws of the expected rates, rebuilt from the posterior parameters and forecast indexes; they carry the uncertainty of the parameters and of the future indexes. Predictive draws add Poisson and extra-Poisson variation of the observed deaths as for other models (for the negative binomial family this takes the place of its overdispersion). Fitted rates are posterior means.

The fit warns when the chains have not converged (largest R-hat of the model parameters above 1.05) or had divergent transitions; then use more iter or chains. Cohort models need single years of age. StanMoMo needs whole numbers: deaths and exposures are rounded (a warning reports rounding of exposures by more than 1%). Fits take from seconds to minutes per stratum; cores runs the chains in parallel.

References

Barigou K, Goffard P-O, Loisel S, Salhi Y (2023). Bayesian model averaging for mortality forecasting using leave-future-out validation. International Journal of Forecasting 39(2): 674-690. doi:10.1016/j.ijforecast.2022.01.011

See also

stmomo() for the same models fitted by maximum likelihood.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("StanMoMo", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 2000:2019)
  fit <- mt_fit(stanmomo("lc", chains = 1, iter = 400, h_max = 10), x)
  fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 10, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
}
# }
